A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MeasureBench study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, and revised content.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 17 VLMs, thinking-mode comparisons, GRPO training experiments, numerical-output analyses, and tests of traditional gauge-reading systems.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds prompt experiments, supervised fine-tuning comparisons, general-benchmark evaluations, and GRPO results for a 3B model.

M1.justification: The registry-based 2D/3D synthesis pipeline, GRPO procedure, correctness-plus-format reward, and soft-margin alternative remain substantively unchanged. Moving the soft-margin reward to Appendix A.2 and applying GRPO to another model size do not introduce a new proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluations on MMMU, MMMU-Pro, MathVista, and TextVQA to test retention of broader capabilities (Table 5), substantially extending task coverage beyond instrument reading. MeasureBench itself retains the same 2,442 examples and instrument coverage; the synthetic-type count of 17 in v1 Section 2.4 becomes 16, consistent with Table 1 in both versions.

E2.justification: v2 introduces answer-only and rationale-based SFT as substantive training comparators to GRPO (Table 6). It also adds Qwen3-VL-8B to the main and thinking comparisons and GPT-4.1-Mini to prompt experiments. The traditional systems were already evaluated in v1 Appendix A.7; v2 Table 7 retains them and adds Qwen3-VL-8B to that comparison.

E3.justification: New protocols compare general versus instrument-specific prompts, with and without a precision suffix, excluding 10.53% of prompts deemed immutable. v2 also tests detailed instructions, two SFT response formats, and GRPO on Qwen2.5-VL-3B. The existing GRPO training budget remains 3,900 synthetic examples and 15 epochs. These additions do not establish that retained experiments used changed settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds prompt-sensitivity and instructional-guidance analyses, SFT-versus-GRPO transfer comparisons, checks for degradation on general benchmarks, per-instrument training gains, and a before/after analysis of the clock-time bias. Integer-output diagnostics expand across model families, while v1's [0,1] distribution panels are removed. The soft-margin ablation is retained in the appendix.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The expanded numerical-output distributions describe model behavior rather than introducing uncertainty estimation for performance results.

E6.justification: New prompt, SFT, general-benchmark, and 3B-model results substantially expand the evidence. Retained scores also change: Gemini-2.5-Pro's real/synthetic overall accuracy becomes 30.2/26.3 instead of 30.3/26.1, and Qwen2.5-VL-7B becomes 14.6/10.9 instead of 15.5/11.0. Its GRPO real-world score changes from 20.1 to 19.7. Clock-bias and traditional-system results also change; the PDFs do not explain all revisions to retained scores.

T1.justification: v2 rewrites the existing reward using indicator notation and alpha = 0.9, while retaining the same interval-distance, margin, and partial-credit definitions. Relocating the soft-margin equations does not change their mathematics. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain MeasureBench, controllable synthesis, evidence of fine-grained perception failures, and preliminary synthetic-data training gains with limited real-world transfer. Although v2's abstract describes transfer more positively, its introduction and conclusion retain the qualification. The expanded experiments principally strengthen evidence for the existing contribution scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning SFT overfitting, limited benefits from procedural instructions, stronger RFT gains on simpler instruments, and mitigation of clock-time priors. The electricity-meter case changes from faulting left-to-right reading to accepting the procedure and attributing failure to pointer localization (v1 Appendix A.1 versus v2 D.1). It also removes v1's inference that similar model ordering establishes strong synthetic-to-real transferability.

D1.justification: v2 identifies FlagEvalMM for evaluation and verl for training, specifies GPT-5.2-generated SFT rationales, and discloses avoidance of real clock images showing 10:10 and uniform synthetic clock-time sampling. It also mentions code releases while retaining the project-page address. These disclosures do not establish changes to the existing dataset or implementation; the main GRPO hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for FlagEvalMM and HybridFlow, plus formal citations for previously discussed benchmarks including MMBench, MM-Vet, SEED-Bench, MathVision, and MathVerse. The central positioning against fragmented, instrument-specific evaluations remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The document undergoes substantial reorganization: the traditional-system comparison moves into Section 3.8, reward design and training results receive separate subsections, and the former Appendix A.1–A.7 is reorganized into Appendices A–F. The introduction and synthesis description are condensed and rewritten, and distribution analysis is redistributed between the main text and appendices.

P2.justification: v1 Tables 2 and 3 are merged into v2 Table 2, and the synthesis schematic and example figures are combined. v2 adds experimental tables and an instrument-gain bar chart, redraws distribution plots, reorders the category heatmap, and revises electricity-meter annotations. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering and numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support by testing alternative explanations that v1 left largely unexamined: prompt wording, procedural guidance, and whether synthetic-data gains depend on GRPO rather than SFT (Tables 3, 4, and 6). General-benchmark checks and another trained model size further strengthen the training analysis. These gains outweigh localized reporting weaknesses: Table 7 repeats full-benchmark VLM scores despite describing a dial-meter subset, leaving comparison scope unclear, and Section 3.6 claims no degradation although Table 5 shows small MathVista and TextVQA declines.
